bug_semantics: When Angular SSR trusts X-Forwarded-Prefix, its blacklist validator examines the raw header and rejects literal dot segments but accepts percent-encoded traversal such as /%2e%2e/evil. Subsequent URL and application processing decodes the traversal-bearing prefix; redirect construction can therefore emit an attacker-steered Location and SSR relative HttpClient resolution can be steered to unintended paths or endpoints, subject to the advisory's proxy-header and application-behavior preconditions.
flaw_origin: Commit f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323 first added the advisory-relevant internal X-Forwarded-Prefix validator, INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX /^[/\\]{2}|(?:^|[/\\])\.\.?(?:[/\\]|$)/. It tests the undecoded string for literal slash/backslash and dot segments and neither decodes the header before validation nor applies a safe-path allowlist, so encoded dots bypass it. This is the canonical mainline first-write; the same change was separately backported to supported branches.

reasoning: The published advisory is real and its mechanism is a percent-encoding bypass of Angular SSR's internal X-Forwarded-Prefix validation. Exact-history search and patch inspection locate the smallest canonical first-write of that flawed validator at f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323: it adds a raw-string blacklist for literal dot segments while the parent already has consumers that can use the header in redirect/application URL processing. The immediate parent lacks both the regex and its X-Forwarded-Prefix check, establishing parent-tree absence of the vulnerable lines. This ordinary commit is not a squash and has no reconstructable member layer. Mainline fix 5adc92541433be23fc2246db5a199cf5c0dc9e67 replaces the blacklist with a safe-path allowlist and makes proxy-header trust explicit; the corresponding branch commits align exactly with all four patched release boundaries. Finally, the AI judgment is made only from the BIC commit object: Alan Agius is both human author and committer and there is no AI marker or trailer, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
